description: Phalanx Madrone exterior camera seams — operator-ratified 2026-09-14 (rev 2, 13 cameras)
_readme: A SEAM is an adjacency: a person leaving camera A can plausibly appear next on camera B.
Seams let the system treat several sightings as ONE tracked walk instead of several alerts.
A WRONG seam merges two different people into one track and SUPPRESSES the second alert
(a silent security failure). A MISSING seam only fragments one person into noisier alerts.
So: when unsure, leave a seam OUT. Errors of omission are loud; errors of admission are silent.
Edit this file, then press the reload button (or restart). Any validation error rejects the
WHOLE file and keeps the previous good graph — it never partially applies.
_ring_note: Left-to-right sweep of the main structure, wrapping back to the start. back_yard is on a SEPARATE detached garage and points INTO it.
_skips_note: Operator-validated shortcuts between cameras 2-3 ring positions apart whose fields of view overlap.
_fenced_note: Struck as physically impossible. Listed so re-adding one is an ERROR, not a silent drop. back_yard<->front_side_ptz is additionally refuted by measurement: its cameras' simultaneity is BELOW chance, 32% of its 'hops' complete in under 5 seconds, and it manufactured ~6.6 false circling tracks per day.
_close_pairs_note: Pairs the operator marked as 'not a big transition' — near-identical vantage points. CARRIED BUT NOT YET CONSUMED. Candidate future use: count a close pair as ONE camera toward the 3-distinct-camera circling threshold, so loitering at one doorway seen by two overlapping cameras cannot fake a circling event.
_egress_note: NOT every egress camera is exterior. The garage cameras watch a way INTO the house but sit inside the garage and do not normally see external people — they must NOT appear in the ring. The egress-ADJACENT set is DERIVED from the EXTERIOR list only; never hand-maintain it.
